business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia - United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force since 2012)
Colombia - European Union Free Trade Agreement and Additional Protocol (applied since 2013)
Colombia - United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (in force since 2011)
Colombia - Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty and Colombia - Spain Double Taxation Agreement
Colombia - Switzerland Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Taxation Agreement
Colombia - Canada Free Trade Agreement with Investment Chapter (in force since 2011)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement and Additional Protocol (Mexico, Chile, Peru)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Political Constitution of Colombia (1991); Law 1258 of 2008 (SAS regime); Law 526 of 1999 as amended by Law 1121 of 2006 and subsequent decrees (UIAF AML/CFT framework); Law 1762 of 2015 (transnational bribery and AML extension); Decree 1674 of 2016 (UBO identification rules for supervised entities); Law 2120 of 2021 (AML/CFT modernization and FIU strengthening); Decree 830 of 2021 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB; mandatory registration with DIAN for all legal entities); Superintendencia de Sociedades External Circular 100-000005 of 2022 (SAGRILAFT regime); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular Básica Jurídica (External Circular 029 of 2014) and Chapter I of Circular Externa 100-000000 of 1995 (SARO and AML/SARLAFT regimes applicable to payment and card issuers). UBO reporting threshold: 5% of capital or voting rights, direct or indirect, plus full identification of control chains.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by each foreign shareholder and UBO to the local incorporation attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport of each individual shareholder, UBO, and proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent immigration authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or certificate of incorporation) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record certificate for each UBO and the proposed legal representative (issued within 90 days of application)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation letter and source-of-funds statement covering the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution of the shareholder, with notarized officer signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory documented screening of all shareholders, UBOs, legal representatives, and material counterparties against OFAC SDN and sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Colombian Lista Clinton (narco-trafficking), Consejo de Seguridad Nacional (CONSA) designations, SIGEP Colombian PEP database, UIAF operational alerts and reports of suspicious transactions, INTERPOL Red Notices, and cross-references to the Colombian Criminal Code sanctioned crimes. Screening must be completed pre-mandate, re-run before Chamber of Commerce registration, before SFC licensing, and continuously every 12 months or upon any material ownership change, with results archived in the SAGRILAFT compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) - official portal www.rue.com.co, operated jointly by the Cámaras de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), which issues the name-clearance certificate (certificado de homonimia / certificado de uso de razón social).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish or a Spanish-transliterated Latin-script form; the name must be pronounceable and legible in Spanish; only Spanish corporate abbreviations are permitted (e.g., S.A.S.); foreign words or trademarks may be incorporated if transliterated and not contrary to public order, morality, or legal restrictions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RUES certificate of homonimia is valid for 30 calendar days; the reservation may be renewed once for a further 30-day period through the same RUES portal before expiry, otherwise a new clearance request is required. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) before the issuing Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days of notification, and a subsidiary administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) to the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same period if the ground is legal. In parallel, the applicant should prepare and submit at least three alternative names, each requiring a new RUES availability certificate; the clearance is non-transferable and tied to the specific entity structure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. For the initial SAS incorporation, the registered office may be a legalized commercial address, including a licensed serviced-office or virtual-office address accepted by the Chamber of Commerce. However, for the target activity (virtual expense-card issuing and spend-management under the supervision of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia), the licensee must maintain a physical operational and compliance presence in Colombia, including board governance records, SAGRILAFT/AML-CFT filing archives, and a compliance officer; a mail-forwarding-only virtual address will not satisfy commercial-substance tests for the SFC license or the SAGRILAFT regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: estimated 62-68% probability (midpoint approximately 65%) of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, UIAF, or DIAN within the first 18 months following licensing, reflecting the high-risk ISIC 6619 payment-processing AML tier; formation-stage inspections are uncommon but documentary audits and name-clearance verification visits by the Chamber of Commerce may occur.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUES name-availability consultation and certificate of homonimia
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of incorporation (estatutos) with ISIC 6619 scope clause
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed-fee benchmark (USD 250-450 per hour equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of shareholder signatures on the private incorporation document
Hague Apostille certification for up to five foreign shareholder and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of origin (or designated apostille authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document consular tariff (average USD 50 per certificate; varies by origin jurisdiction)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents (statutory, passport, good standing, criminal record, bank letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately USD 8-12 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial Chamber of Commerce registration (matrícula mercantil) and RUES filing for the SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff based on minimum capital class

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUB (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) initial filing with DIAN by licensed public accountant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee; annual filing obligation included in retainer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAGRILAFT pre-incorporation AML/CFT compliance manual, UBO risk matrix, and PEP screening report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee; mandatory prior to SFC licensing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Criminal background certificate (Policía Nacional) and disciplinary background certificate (Procuraduría) for the proposed legal representative and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Policía Nacional de Colombia / Procuraduría General de la Nación

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-licensing legal opinion and SFC pre-consultation memorandum on virtual-card issuing under ISIC 6619
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for SFC pre-consultation support

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Colombian Code of Commerce (Código de Comercio) Arts. 110–127 and 372–373; Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime) Arts. 1–7, 12, 21; Decree 2555 of 2010 Part 1 Title 3 (SEDPE licensing regime)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Único Empresarial (RUES), under the functional oversight of the Superintendencia de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) authenticated before the Chamber of Commerce and registered in RUES; public deed (Escritura Pública) executed before a Notario Público is mandatory where real property is contributed or where Law 1258/2008 Art. 5 so requires
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the S.A.S. regime; capital is freely fixed in the bylaws. However, the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) requires fully paid-up equity of approximately COP 500,000,000 (approx. USD 130,000, indexed) for the SEDPE virtual-card operating license, evidenced by a bank certification of the funds held in a Colombian regulated financial institution and maintained during the entity's operation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscribers' share subscription plan is hereby approved; each subscriber's capital contributions shall be paid pursuant to the terms of the incorporation document and credited as of this date. (2) The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and the legal representative is empowered to execute the lease and obtain the municipal zoning certificate. (3) The following officers are appointed: [Name], Legal Representative (Representante Legal Principal); [Name], Alternate Legal Representative; and [Name], Company Secretary, each with the powers set forth in the bylaws, including opening bank accounts and initiating the SEDPE licensing application before the Financial Superintendence. (4) All filings are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed Colombian S.A.S. corporate names through the RUES homonimia module. Obtain the Certificado de Homonimia confirming that none of the proposed names is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. The certificate is valid for 30 calendar days; reserve the selected name immediately and proceed to the constitutional instrument.
required_dossiers: RUES online name-search request form
Identity documents (cédula or passport copies) of all incorporators
Payment receipt of the nominal homonimia search tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber denies all proposed names, resubmit alternative denominations; if the answer is delayed beyond the SLA, file a written request for expedited resolution; disputes may be escalated to the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública in Bogotá (public-deed route) or authorized direct execution by incorporators (private-document route)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the S.A.S. bylaws, authorized/subscribed/paid capital schedule, corporate purpose expressly covering electronic payment services and virtual corporate card issuance, and corporate governance rules. Where real property is contributed, the instrument must be risen to a public deed before a Notary; otherwise, the private document must be signed by all shareholders and authenticated for subsequent Chamber registration.
required_dossiers: Final S.A.S. incorporation instrument and bylaws
Certificado de Homonimia
Identity documents of all subscribing shareholders
SAGRILAFT preliminary self-assessment and supporting background information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary requires additional legalization of foreign shareholder documents, obtain apostille or consular legalization; any drafting defect is cured by executing an amendment (aclaración) before the same Notary or re-executing the private instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration with the Chamber of Commerce (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed incorporation instrument and the completed Formulario Único de Registro (FUR) through RUES. Pay the registration tariff calculated on declared registered assets. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (C.E.R.L.), which is the conclusive proof of the S.A.S.'s legal existence, corporate representation, and registered officers.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation document (private or public deed)
FUR – Formulario Único de Registro and RUES submission acknowledgment
Payment receipt of the registration tariff
Matrícula mercantil declaration and asset statement
Electronic notification consent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber raises an objection (e.g., deficient capital table or unregistered object clause), cure the defect and re-present within 10 working days; any final rejection may be appealed within 5 working days to the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the C.E.R.L., complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) registration online with the DIAN. Select the ordinary income-tax regime, VAT status (responsable/I.V.A. if applicable), withholding-agent classification, and the Bogotá D.C. business address. The legal representative's digital certificate must be created to enable electronic invoicing and subsequent tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (C.E.R.L.)
Certified copy of the legal representative's appointment
Identity document of the legal representative
Proof of business address (lease agreement or utility invoice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the RUT filing, correct the electronic form and resubmit; where the legal representative is a foreign resident, obtain the municipal address validation certificate before presenting; any erroneous classification may be rectified via the online RUT correction procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SEDPE operating license application before the Financial Superintendence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) — Ventanilla Única de Atención / Trámites en Línea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorization application to operate as a Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) under Decree 2555 of 2010. Submit the corporate charter, SAGRILAFT/AML manual, information security policy aligned with SFC Circulars, a complete B2B virtual corporate card business plan, sponsor-bank or card network (Mastercard/Visa) program agreements, and the bank certification of paid-up equity. Respond to all SFC information requirements within the granted deadline and obtain the authorization resolution prior to commencing card-issuing operations.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation documents and C.E.R.L.
Company RUT and tax standing certificate
SAGRILAFT and money-laundering risk management manual
B2B virtual card business plan with KYC/KYB and spend-control framework
IT security audit report and third-party processor contracts
Bank certificate of the paid-up equity (approx. COP 500,000,000)
Integrity and background statements for legal representatives and board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SFC issues a formal objection (requerimiento), cure within the imposed deadline; where the application is denied, rectify the objected elements and re-file; the denial may be challenged through the procedural remedies of reposición and apelación before the SFC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC), jointly with the Superintendencia de Sociedades for corporate oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Funcionamiento para Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) for electronic deposit and virtual corporate card issuance, together with card program authorizations under the SFC's Circular Básica Jurídica (Circular 029/2014)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) / Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) for office premises in Bogotá D.C.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Full EIA not required for an office-only fintech operational configuration; a simplified environmental registration may apply for hazardous and electronic waste generation under Resolution 2184/2019, with a post-consumer e-waste program (Decreto 284/2018) if card terminals and IT hardware are decommissioned.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic sanitary wastewater only: compliance with Resolution 631/2015 Table 2 (COD ≤ 800 mg/L; TSS ≤ 400 mg/L) for indirect municipal sewer discharge; VOC emission limits not applicable in the absence of industrial processes; electronic waste handling must follow Decree 284/2018 and Resolution 1512/2010 for computers and peripherals, including collection agreements with certified recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) issued by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogotá for the registered office; structural compliance with the NSR-10 (Norma Sismo Resistente 2010) seismic design requirements for the leased premises; occupational health and safety clearance through the company's SG-SST system filed under Resolution 0312/2019 with the Ministerio de Trabajo and the affiliated ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales); civil-defense evacuation and emergency response plans must be documented and submitted to the local disaster risk management office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax and Customs Directorate (DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales), virtual portal at https://muisca.dian.gov.co; institutional site at https://www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or domestic legal entity must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and registration in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario). For a newly incorporated Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.), the NIT is assigned automatically during Chamber of Commerce registration; the legal representative must then update the RUT through the DIAN Muisca portal using a current digital certificate. A non-resident entity not otherwise required to create a local branch may, through an appointed agent or representative, obtain a simplified NIT/RUT for purposes of Colombian withholding tax and non-resident VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide a US-style check-the-box pass-through election. The S.A.S. is in all cases classified as a Colombian income-tax resident legal entity, taxed at the entity level. Elective regimes are limited to practical alternatives such as the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' for eligible small businesses, free-zone taxation under Article 240-1 of the Tax Code, and consolidated tax-group treatment only for parent-controlled entities under Law 1819 of 2016. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied statutorily through transfer-pricing and deduction-denial provisions, not through a taxpayer-selected classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for legal entities performing taxable activities; all such entities must obtain RUT and charge VAT from inception. The de minimis threshold for natural persons is 42,000 UVT (COP 1,976,772,000 for 2024 at UVT 47,066), subject to additional conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies to all VAT taxpayers. Invoices are generated through DIAN-authorized software integrators and transmitted to DIAN's real-time fiscal validation system via API in XML format, with a digital signature, CUFE/CUDS code, and QR stamp. Exports require the electronic invoice to be associated with customs export declarations and the exporter's RUT status.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods and services may be zero-rated (0% IVA) when: (i) the taxpayer is registered as an exporter in the RUT; (ii) goods physically leave Colombia under a customs export declaration; or (iii) services satisfy Article 481 of the Tax Code, i.e., the service is rendered in Colombia to an offshore beneficiary, used exclusively outside Colombia, and the supporting contract and invoicing evidence the foreign use. For B2B virtual card and payment technology services, zero-rating is available where the card issuer provides the service exclusively to non-resident merchants or cardholders and the economic exploitation takes place outside Colombia.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX / Declaración de Exportación)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Channeling Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro / Formulario No. 5)
Export service contract and supporting technical documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN reviews export zero-rating claims against the DEX system, foreign-exchange channeling records, and beneficiary status. Fraudulent or unjustified zero-rating gives rise to retrospective VAT collection with default interest, penalty surcharges under Articles 647 and 648 of the Tax Code up to 200% of the omitted tax amount, monetary correction, cancellation of the exporter/RUT status, and criminal liability for tax fraud under recent anti-abuse legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for prudential oversight and the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit for policy coordination
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is convertible but subject to a managed foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions, including import payments, services, interest, and royalties, are freely transferable through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, securities investment, and cross-border loans, are permitted but must be routed through authorized intermediaries and registered with Banco de la República via the Declaración de Cambio system. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are permitted upon satisfactory tax compliance, including dividend withholding tax, and are executed through an authorized bank using the appropriate exchange code; no general exchange control approval is required for such remittances once the underlying foreign investment has been properly registered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds arising from goods and services must be repatriated to Colombia and settled in the foreign exchange market through an authorized intermediary, either by sale to the local market or by deposit into a foreign-currency account maintained with a local commercial bank. The general statutory term for repatriation and settlement is six months from the date of the export declaration, loading, or the contractual term of collection, subject to extensions granted by Banco de la República in specific regulated circumstances such as deferred payments or special regimes. Mandatory conversion of export proceeds is the default, although exporters may retain balances in foreign currency accounts up to the applicable regulatory thresholds for subsequent operational needs.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for fully offshore or non-licensed digital EMI service providers. Colombia does not recognize the EU/UK-style EMI license. Any entity issuing a virtual card or providing electronic payment services to Colombian residents must obtain authorization from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, generally as a Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPE) or as a financial institution authorized for payment systems. A foreign cross-border EMI may operate only through an approved local subsidiary, a joint venture with a locally licensed entity, or an outsourcing/correspondent arrangement with a Colombian banking partner. Legal constraints prohibit the direct issuance of payment instruments by an unlicensed foreign entity without a local regulated presence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors must provide, in principle, remote onboarding capability through digital identity verification and electronic signatures. However, for a high-risk fintech virtual card issuer, the Colombian bank's compliance framework will typically require an in-person or videoconference KYC interview with the final legal representatives and beneficial owners. Enhanced due diligence mandates include the presentation of original or notarized corporate documents, proof of identity of all UBOs, source of wealth and source of funds documentation, and a clear explanation of the card issuing model and liquidity flows. In practice, a physical visit by at least one senior manager to the bank's corporate center is often mandatory for account activation and to establish a durable compliance relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership, including layered ownership across multiple non-resident jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate organizational chart demonstrating direct and indirect ownership; apostilled certificates of incorporation and registry certificates for each entity layer; national identity cards and passports of UBOs; comprehensive declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, supported by audited financial statements, tax filings, bank references, and professional legal opinions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the projected transaction volume, low transaction values, and the expected liquidity requirements of a virtual card issuer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and projected cash-flow model; executed agreements with card network partners and merchant acquirers; transactional monitoring and anti-fraud procedures; tiered transaction limits and velocity controls; KYC/AML policies for cardholders and merchants; and evidence of a local compliance officer with formal reporting lines to the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern that the entity is a shell company with no real economic substance in Colombia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office lease agreements; payroll records and social security filings for local employees; board resolutions evidencing decisions made in Colombia; copies of commercial contracts with Colombian counterparties; Colombian tax registration (RUT) and periodic tax returns; and records of substantive operational activity, including software, compliance, and customer support operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate controls or prohibited connections to crypto-assets or unregulated payment corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on crypto-asset acceptance or settlement; banking relationship documentation covering all partner and service-provider accounts; a schedule of approved counterparties with license verification; independent audit evidence of transaction monitoring software; and a third-party AML/CFT review or certification demonstrating compliance with Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular Básica Jurídica requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or subordinated debt capital must be transferred via SWIFT MT103 from the parent entity to the Colombian entity's local capital escrow or operational account using the purpose code corresponding to 'Direct Foreign Investment' in the Declaración de Cambio. The wire must include a complete beneficiary bank account name and number, the entity's NIT (tax ID), and the remit reference: 'Aporte de capital social' or 'Contrato de préstamo externo', as applicable. The Colombian recipient bank generates the mandatory foreign exchange declaration to Banco de la República. The capital injection must be registered under the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales within the statutory period to preserve the investor's right to later remit profits and capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments are executed through the local banking system using SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier transfers, documentary commercial letters of credit for structured import settlements, and potentially bank-accepted drafts or collection instructions. Each disbursement must be supported by the underlying commercial invoice or pro-forma contract and filed as a Declaración de Cambio through the intermediary. For settlement of card network liabilities (Mastercard or Visa), the Colombian entity clears net payable positions in USD through its correspondent banks or directly with the network's settlement bank in the United States, then settles the resulting COP liability with the local bank through the foreign exchange market.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore COP/USD deliverable forward contracts sold by authorized local banks
COP/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with local or permitted foreign counterparties, limited to hedging of real commercial or financial exposures
Cross-currency swaps between COP and USD for term-aligned currency risk management
FX options produced by authorized intermediary banks for transaction-specific hedges, subject to the General Financial Network License

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the mercantile registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the principal domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar window: 1 January through 31 March each year; no extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after 31 March triggers a 15% surcharge on the base tariff plus a per-month penalty (approx. USD 10-20); sustained non-renewal results in loss of ‘renovada’ status, unavailability of clean existence certificates, and, after verified cessation of activity, administrative cancellation of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary shareholders' meeting minutes approving annual financial statements and dividend policy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (registration of the acta in the Commercial Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held no later than 31 March following the fiscal year-end; minutes registered with the Chamber within 30 days of the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts by 31 March exposes the entity to a Chamber fine of up to 4 SMMLV (approx. USD 1,050) and potential intervention by the Superintendency of Companies; unregistered minutes are ineffective against third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified annual financial statements and statutory auditor's report (dictamen del Revisor Fiscal) filed for public registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; additionally Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for licensed card-issuing entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts closed at 31 December; filed with the Chamber by 30 April of the following year or within 30 days of assembly approval; SFC-supervised filings due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of financial statements attracts administrative fines of up to 4 SMMLV before the Chamber and separate SFC fines of up to 2,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 670,000); materially false statements expose the legal representative to criminal false-return liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and complementary return (Formulario 110) with corporate income tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax and Customs Directorate (DIAN), electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December; return due between late July and mid-September of the following year (e.g., fiscal year 2024: 26 July - 10 September 2025), allocated by the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized at 5% of tax due per month of delay (capped at 100%) plus default interest; non-filing enables DIAN official assessment with penalties ranging from 100% to 160% of omitted tax and asset-seizure procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) - UBO declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (RUB module of the taxpayer digital portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 February and 31 May following the monitored year; extraordinary update required within 30 days of any share transfer or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or false beneficial-owner information incurs a penalty under E.T. Article 651 of up to 15,000 UVT (approx. USD 4,300) plus monthly late surcharge; repeated non-compliance blocks issuance of compliance certificates and tax clean statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) annual consolidated return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal revenue authority of the operational domicile (e.g., Bogotá D.C., Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due in March/April of the year following the taxable period; bimonthly or quarterly prepayments are made during the period and reconciled in the final annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 5% per-month late surcharge (capped at 100%) plus default interest; repeated non-payment may result in account embargoes and, for licensed activities, suspension of the municipal operating permit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual periodic financial and compliance reporting to the financial supervisor (Información anual SFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March for the 31 December year-end; supplementary quarterly operational data filed in the SFC reporting portal during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or misreporting is subject to SFC fines of up to 2,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 670,000); persistent non-compliance can lead to revocation of the virtual-card issuing and payment-entity authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit and Revisor Fiscal are required when (i) gross assets exceed 5,000 UVT (approx. COP 235 million / USD 60,000 for 2024), (ii) gross annual revenue exceeds 3,000 UVT (approx. COP 141 million / USD 36,000), or (iii) the entity is engaged in, or licensed for, card-issuing or payment activity under SFC supervision - the virtual corporate card issuer scope triggers the mandate regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS (NIIF) as incorporated by Decree 2420/2015 applies to SFC-supervised entities and qualifying large companies (Grupo 1); IFRS for SMEs (Grupo 2) applies to non-supervised mid-size SAS; financial statements are presented in COP with notes, certified by the legal representative and a registered public accountant.
